name: Circular Intersection (Roundabout)
spec: yellow diamond with three black arrows forming a counter-clockwise circle
meaning: A roundabout ahead; slow down and yield to traffic already in the circle.

snippets.back: Roundabout traffic travels counterclockwise around a central island, and entering traffic must yield to traffic already circulating.
A roundabout is a circular intersection, usually without a traffic signal, where traffic travels counter-clockwise around a central island.
Slow when approaching a roundabout; the manual describes typical design speeds of about fifteen to twenty miles per hour.
You enter a roundabout from the right, yielding to vehicles already circulating, and follow the circle to the right until you reach your road.
Enter a roundabout to the right of its central island when there is a suitable gap.
Roundabouts are spreading in the U.S. because one-way counterclockwise flow creates fewer conflict points and moves traffic more safely and efficiently than standard intersections.
Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists in a roundabout and to those crossing at its marked exit crosswalk.

Compared with other intersection controls, roundabouts cut fatal crashes about ninety percent, injury crashes about seventy-five percent and all crashes about thirty-five percent, according to the crash statistics the manual cites.
